Fix four open review findings on PR #523 (change 321, branch `dependabot/cargo/oxc-92353111ed`, head 33b492b9, trail 492) in the caliper repo with ONE class fix. This is the third round of 'a form main detected is now dropped': stop spot-fixing. In your worktree: `git fetch origin`, `git switch -c fix-oxc7 origin/dependabot/cargo/oxc-92353111ed`; push with `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/dependabot/cargo/oxc-92353111ed` (normal fast-forward; NEVER force; if dependabot moved the branch, fetch and merge). You OWN crates/core/src/extractor/** and crates/core/src/resolver/callee.rs; touch nothing else (#527 edits dependency_types.rs, pipeline/*, crates/semantic/**). Read first: /Users/gabe/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-caliper/memory/worker-contract.md, evidence-types-direction.md and diagnose-after-three-findings.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md ('Absence is not evidence', 'A test varies what it claims'), `gh pr view 523`, rounds 4-6 (commits 40fc068c, fbd83a0d, 33b492b9: one linear peel, `Peeled`, evidence Identity/Reference/NoComponent/NotRenderable/Unknown). Rules: signed commits with trailer `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED`; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` first; one cargo process at a time; scratch under /tmp/claude-501/; update the PR body FILE /tmp/claude-501/pr-oxc.md in place ('Review round 7'; keep what is true) and the changeset; I publish the body and resolve findings. Final message max 170 words: head SHA, the rule, each finding CONFIRMED (failing test on 33b492b9)/refuted, blockers. Cap 120 tool calls; never ask questions. THE FINDINGS (each a form origin/main (oxc 0.158) detected and we now drop; verify with a failing test on 33b492b9; if one is already fixed at this head, say so with the test): (A) medium: `(rows as { map(render: (row: string) => React.ReactNode): any[] }).map(row => {row})` returned from a typed component: `any[]` is treated as definitely non-renderable, so `rendered_callee` hides `map` before evidence.rs ~143-156 visits its callback and the typed-function check fails (component.rs ~934-937): `any[]` must be inconclusive. (B) medium: `(ui as { withContext

(View: React.ComponentType

): React.FC

}).withContext(Base)` used to document the result with `PublicProps` but now loses the component: the alias path defers to the explicit props argument (component.rs ~1406-1409) and a guard then prevents `promote_wrapper_calls` (wrapper.rs ~282-325) from using it only because the original callee declaration is unavailable: keep the candidate with `callee: None` so the explicit props still resolve without the original signature. (C) medium: `(React as { createElement(tag: 'div'): { type: string; props: {}; key: string | null } }).createElement('div')` returned from a typed component is skipped though the result is structurally a ReactElement: classifying every non-callable object literal as NotRenderable removes `createElement` before the factory check (evidence.rs ~142-146): structurally element-compatible object types must be inconclusive. (D) low: `parse_file` runs an AST walk and builds a declaration table even with no top-level `typeof` alias (mod.rs ~229-231): collect candidates first and skip when empty; round 6 reports it fixed with a counter test: confirm on 33b492b9 and say so. THE ROOT: `NotRenderable` is an open-ended, syntax-shaped classifier ('every non-callable object literal', 'any[]', ...) so each new type shape the extractor did not anticipate becomes hard evidence against a real component. THE RULE (implement it as the ONLY way to produce NotRenderable): NotRenderable comes ONLY from a small CLOSED list of types that TypeScript itself cannot assign to `ReactNode | ComponentType | ReactElement` under any generic instantiation, decided by the asserted type's own syntax with no resolution: the keyword types `object`, `symbol`, `void` (and `bigint` only if you can justify it against ReactNode; say so), and a function/call-signature whose result is one of those; everything else, including `any[]`, `unknown[]`, arrays, tuples, type references, object literals with or without call signatures, unions/intersections containing anything outside the list, mapped/conditional/indexed types, `never`, generics, is Unknown. Write the list as ONE exhaustive match over the TS type-node enum with NO wildcard arm (a new type node kind must fail to compile and be placed), each arm commented with why. Then B: a wrapper candidate whose callee signature is unavailable keeps the candidate (`callee: None`) rather than being dropped, wherever the guard in wrapper.rs lives; grep every consumer of the guard. TESTS: failing-first per finding with exact assertions; the NO-RECALL-REGRESSION DIFFERENTIAL (extend wrapper_matrix_tests.rs / the 407-row recall table from origin/main): add a RETURN-TYPE axis crossing every detection form with these asserted result types: any, any[], unknown, unknown[], object, symbol, void, never, string, number, null, boolean, ReactNode, ReactElement, JSX.Element, FC

, ComponentType

, an element-shaped object literal `{type; props; key}`, an empty object literal `{}`, an object literal with a call signature returning each of these, a union with each, an intersection with each, a generic `T`, an indexed access, a conditional type: assert every row the BASE detected is still detected unless its asserted result is exactly in the closed list (name the row and the list entry); add the reverse test: each closed-list entry still declines. Mutation-prove the closed list (adding a type to it, removing one, adding a wildcard arm). ---
name: worker-contract
description: "Rules every caliper worker follows (scope, branch/push, targeted checks, call cap, PR body, pre-push gate). Copied from the deleted caliper-fixtures/worker-contract.md on 2026-11-17; paths to fixtures no longer exist"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 6f993b0f-3007-4088-bd26-63eda356278e
  modified: 2026-11-18T01:13:52.369Z
---

Restored from my reading of `~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/worker-contract.md` (deleted by the user 2026-11-17; see [[fixtures-is-not-scratch]]). Changes made while restoring: no build output or scratch in `caliper-fixtures`; PR bodies go in `$TMPDIR` or the worktree, not there.

**Scope**: edit only the files the brief names; if another must change, stop and say which and why. Never ask the user questions; if blocked, report what blocks and what you tried. Do not wait on background work.

**Branch and push**: branch from origin/main unless the brief says otherwise. Build in the worktree's own `target/` (the `just test-checker-lane` recipe hard-wires `$PWD/target/release`). Plain `rustc` is 1.99.1 here; the old note about the mise shim forcing 1.98.1 did not reproduce on 2026-11-17. Signed commits ending `Claude-Session: <session url>`. Push normally (`git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>`, fully qualified when pushing a bare SHA), never `--no-verify`, verify the remote SHA with `git ls-remote`. Workers do not open or edit the PR and do not poll CI.

**Checks, targeted (CI runs the rest)**: always before push `just lint doc-check machete typos`. Then only what the change touches: Rust -> nextest of touched crates; types/output/merge -> `just test-checker-lane` once (run it without a CARGO_TARGET_DIR override); checker/session code -> gate_harness determinism and memory modes; output-preserving change -> full-content diff (JSON parsed, `stats` dropped) of `extract --json --quiet --no-cache` against a build of origin/main on a large fixture and a Chakra-only fixture. Do NOT run deny, semver, test-ts, test-napi, test-integration, test-py unless that area changed. Tests must fail on base for every behavior change. No oracle runs, no corpus fetches. No new scripts, options or recipes. Changeset only if `just semver` demands one. No wall-clock timing unless the brief asks; check `uptime`, prefer allocation or instruction counts.

**Cap**: stop and report after the call cap in the brief (default 60 tool calls) with what is verified; "not done, because X" beats burning calls.

**Artifacts**: PR body with `## What`, `## Evidence` (numbers, exit codes, what was diffed), `## Not verified`, last line the session url; the lead publishes it unedited. Final message <= 120 words: branch, head SHA (ls-remote verified), body path, blockers.

**Pre-push gate (the reviewer must find nothing new)**:
- Guards are ALLOW-lists: handle a closed set of proven forms; everything else is Unknown/Declined (never "complete", "none", "exact"). No `_ =>` arms in decisions over node/type kinds.
- Write the slice's invariants in the PR body (unknown unless proven; by binding not spelling; every read recorded; one owner; wired or not defined).
- Grammar sweep: list every syntax/type form the code can receive and show each is handled or declined (exhaustive match, or a generated test over the grammar with the checker/TS API as oracle). Generate over the grammar, not over past findings.
- Mutation proof: remove each guard/dependency; a test must fail. Report which you tried (cargo mutants --in-diff works).
- Before reporting: run `/code-review medium` on the explicit SHA range, then try to break your own change with inputs the diff did not mention (computed keys, symbols, getters, overloads, re-exports, shadowing, optional chains, declare/abstract, conditional types, lone surrogates).

Three read-only audits on 2026-11-24 (reports committed on branch `docs/review-checklist` under `docs/audits/2026-11-24-*.md`) found that our recurring review findings are one root problem in three places: a DECISION is made from something that is not evidence. Extractor: a spelling (PascalCase callee, name lists, `contains("Component")`) or a raw expression. Wire boundary (crates/semantic): an ABSENT or defaulted field read as a value (`#[serde(default)]`, `unwrap_or(false)`, tsrs omits empty fields). Caches and sessions: a DEGRADED result (timeout, read failure, heap budget, nesting cut) stored as authoritative. The rules already exist in prose (CONTRIBUTING 'Before you push', ADR 0025-0028: by binding not spelling, one owner per decision, unknown unless proven, always emit a Diagnostic when degrading); nothing enforces them in code.

**Why:** reviews found 3 + 3 + 5 findings per PR in the same classes; each fix moved the problem (validating on a shared cache primed it the other way). Fixing per site does not converge.

**How to apply (direction, in this order):** (1) failing-first counter-example suites (extractor M10: every snippet in the audit becomes a row asserting exact output); (2) make invalid states unrepresentable: `ComponentEvidence` required to build a `ComponentMapping`, a typed `Peeled` (Transparent | Instantiated | Asserted) with one exhaustive match, `Known<T>` for decoded wire fields, a `Degraded` marker on outcomes that no cache or kept answer stores, `CallError::Contract` for undecodable responses with its own code; (3) one owner modules (`extractor/decide.rs`, `semantic/src/wire.rs` with one tsrs version-pin test, one `Memo` abstraction); (4) architecture tests (grep-based Rust tests, no new scripts) that fail on a catch-all arm or a name literal in a decision, `unwrap_or(false)` on wire values, text matching of messages, statics in non-test code; (5) determinism as a tested property: differential tests with separate state per consumer as oracle, session equals cold extract under random edit scripts. Amend ADR 0027/0026: 'a name is a candidate filter, never a verdict'. Related: [[diagnose-after-three-findings]], [[workers-run-full-lint-gate]].

name: diagnose-after-three-findings
description: "After three findings on one PR stop routing spot fixes: tabulate them, name root causes (one decision with two owners, state keyed wrong, singletons), decide if the design must change"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: ad4b3461-bb6f-49f0-bb4d-997d9b8887ba
  modified: 2026-11-16T01:05:54.318Z
---

On 2026-11-14 the user said they were "disappointed that you're not taking a step back to understand the patterns, consider the architecture and our models" after the Storybook live-upgrade PR (#462) collected 11 findings over 5 rounds that I routed one at a time as spot fixes. I had promised a model-based approach "if another finding appears" and still patched the next one.

**Why:** findings arrive serially from a reviewer that sees a slice each round; workers capped at 25-35 calls patch the symptom. The 11 findings shared four root causes: no explicit lifecycle model (state scattered across flags keyed by the wrong dimension: component instead of component+revision+key+client), decisions made in two places (lazy vs eager, structural vs checker diagnostics, two dev servers), last-writer-wins singletons where truth is a per-client set, and TypeScript re-deriving what the Rust core already owns. Same smell as #455 (two walkers decide eligibility), #459 (two paths feed the kept answer), #458.

**How to apply:**
- Third finding on a PR: stop; make a table of the findings, name the root causes, ask 'is one decision made or held in two places?' and 'what is the state machine and who owns it?'.
- Remedy shape: one owner for each decision (prefer the Rust core's merged answer over re-deriving in TS), one explicit reducer (pure state x event -> state x effects), and a model-based/property test of the invariants after quiescence, with the earlier findings as named regression sequences.
- Give such a worker room (cap ~100 calls, Opus); caps suit mechanical work, not stateful mechanisms.
- Before accepting any worker fix ask: is the same fact decided or held anywhere else?

**Second instance, 2026-11-15 (#467, tsrs_module swapped for oxc_resolver):** five findings in five rounds, each in glue code that re-created an old behaviour (symlink canonicalization, `.cts` conditions, relative tsconfig, fingerprint inputs, a `baseUrl` fallback that guessed which rule answered from whether the path contained `node_modules`). I called the root cause settled twice and was wrong twice. The user: "How are you not guarding against these coming up???"

**Why:** a behaviour-preserving library swap was gated by a single-run identity diff on two fixtures, which cannot see cross-run cache staleness or inputs the fixtures lack; fix rounds added new heuristic code that nothing exercised; the Entire reviewer was the first real review. The swap's premise ("same results, less code") was false: tsrs follows TypeScript 7 (no `baseUrl` for bare specifiers) where the old resolver followed TypeScript 6, and the PR grew to +768/-222.

**How to apply:**
- Before a swap: inventory every behaviour of the replaced component that the code relies on (options, conditions, symlinks, config inheritance, cache keys) and diff old against new over the cross-product, not two fixtures.
- Before pushing any worker branch: read the diff myself for heuristics (a rule inferred from path shape, a guess) and run `/code-review` on it; do not let the Entire reviewer be the first review.
- At the third finding re-test the premise (does the swap still delete more than it adds?), not only the root cause; if not, close the PR.

**Third instance, 2026-11-15 (about 50 findings across trails 404/405):** the user said "consider all of the findings together, architecturally and semantically ... make sure the agents won't find even more things". Eight root classes (silence read as evidence, lossy model asserting exactness, spelling instead of binding, derived state outside the dependency model, one decision with two owners, host assumptions, hand-tuned policy with no reference model, contract drift / fields never populated). Table: ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/shrink/findings-synthesis.md.

**Why:** guards were DENY-lists (enumerate the wrong cases found so far), so each new grammar form (a `[Symbol.iterator]` key) produced the next finding; about 40% of the raw count was the same code repeated in stacked child PRs.

**How to apply:**
- Design guards as ALLOW-lists: a closed set of proven forms, everything else Unknown/Declined; exhaustive matches, no wildcard arms in decisions.
- Run the pre-push gate in worker-contract.md (invariants, grammar sweep with the checker/TS API as oracle, mutation proof, adversarial pass, then /code-review) before any push; generate tests over the grammar, not over past findings.
- Merge stacks in order and retarget children; do not keep a stack alive across review rounds.

See [[resolve-findings-when-fixed]] and [[worker-token-budget]].
61:- **Absence is not evidence:** a missing field, flag or declaration does not prove a negative. Settle a negative only on positive evidence, and ask the checker when unsure.
62:- **A test varies what it claims:** change the thing the test is named for (ignore the parameter, drop the wrapper, skip the order) and it must fail. Table-drive over every variant with an exhaustive `match`, so a new variant does not compile until it has a case.
63-- **A dependency bump that changes shapes** (a parser, a checker): diff the output of the old and the new version on all five corpora, and give every form the new version wraps (parentheses, `as`, `satisfies`, `!`, type arguments) a row in one table test through one normalising helper, not a fix per site.
64-- **Findings:** when an automated or human review finds a defect, fix the class it belongs to, not only the case, and resolve the finding with the commit and test that fix it.
65-
66-## Snapshot tests
67-
68-Snapshot tests use [insta](https://insta.rs). Each fixture (shadcn, MUI, Chakra, etc.) has a snapshot of the full extraction output. If your change touches extraction output, insta will flag it:
69-
70-```bash
71-cargo test -p caliper-docgen-core    # fails with "snapshot mismatch"
72-cargo insta review                     # review diffs, accept or reject
73-```

The 11 findings shared four root causes: no explicit lifecycle model (state scattered across flags keyed by the wrong dimension: component instead of component+revision+key+client), decisions made in two places (lazy vs eager, structural vs checker diagnostics, two dev servers), last-writer-wins singletons where truth is a per-client set, and TypeScript re-deriving what the Rust core already owns. Same smell as #455 (two walkers decide eligibility), #459 (two paths feed the kept answer), #458.

**How to apply:**
- Third finding on a PR: stop; make a table of the findings, name the root causes, ask 'is one decision made or held in two places?' and 'what is the state machine and who owns it?'.
- Remedy shape: one owner for each decision (prefer the Rust core's merged answer over re-deriving in TS), one explicit reducer (pure state x event -> state x effects), and a model-based/property test of the invariants after quiescence, with the earlier findings as named regression sequences.
- Give such a worker room (cap ~100 calls, Opus); caps suit mechanical work, not stateful mechanisms.
- Before accepting any worker fix ask: is the same fact decided or held anywhere else?

**Second instance, 2026-11-15 (#467, tsrs_module swapped for oxc_resolver):** five findings in five rounds, each in glue code that re-created an old behaviour (symlink canonicalization, `.cts` conditions, relative tsconfig, fingerprint inputs, a `baseUrl` fallback that guessed which rule answered from whether the path contained `node_modules`). I called the root cause settled twice and was wrong twice. The user: "How are you not guarding against these coming up???"

**Why:** a behaviour-preserving library swap was gated by a single-run identity diff on two fixtures, which cannot see cross-run cache staleness or inputs the fixtures lack; fix rounds added new heuristic code that nothing exercised; the Entire reviewer was the first real review. The swap's premise ("same results, less code") was false: tsrs follows TypeScript 7 (no `baseUrl` for bare specifiers) where the old resolver followed TypeScript 6, and the PR grew to +768/-222.

**How to apply:**
- Before a swap: inventory every behaviour of the replaced component that the code relies on (options, conditions, symlinks, config inheritance, cache keys) and diff old against new over the cross-product, not two fixtures.
- Before pushing any worker branch: read the diff myself for heuristics (a rule inferred from path shape, a guess) and run `/code-review` on it; do not let the Entire reviewer be the first review.
- At the third finding re-test the premise (does the swap still delete more than it adds?), not only the root cause; if not, close the PR.

**Third instance, 2026-11-15 (about 50 findings across trails 404/405):** the user said "consider all of the findings together, architecturally and semantically ... make sure the agents won't find even more things". Eight root classes (silence read as evidence, lossy model asserting exactness, spelling instead of binding, derived state outside the dependency model, one decision with two owners, host assumptions, hand-tuned policy with no reference model, contract drift / fields never populated). Table: ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/shrink/findings-synthesis.md.

**Why:** guards were DENY-lists (enumerate the wrong cases found so far), so each new grammar form (a `[Symbol.iterator]` key) produced the next finding; about 40% of the raw count was the same code repeated in stacked child PRs.

**How to apply:**
- Design guards as ALLOW-lists: a closed set of proven forms, everything else Unknown/Declined; exhaustive matches, no wildcard arms in decisions.
- Run the pre-push gate in worker-contract.md (invariants, grammar sweep with the checker/TS API as oracle, mutation proof, adversarial pass, then /code-review) before any push; generate tests over the grammar, not over past findings.
- Merge stacks in order and retarget children; do not keep a stack alive across review rounds.

See [[resolve-findings-when-fixed]] and [[worker-token-budget]].
61:- **Absence is not evidence:** a missing field, flag or declaration does not prove a negative. Settle a negative only on positive evidence, and ask the checker when unsure.
62:- **A test varies what it claims:** change the thing the test is named for (ignore the parameter, drop the wrapper, skip the order) and it must fail. Table-drive over every variant with an exhaustive `match`, so a new variant does not compile until it has a case.
63-- **A dependency bump that changes shapes** (a parser, a checker): diff the output of the old and the new version on all five corpora, and give every form the new version wraps (parentheses, `as`, `satisfies`, `!`, type arguments) a row in one table test through one normalising helper, not a fix per site.
64-- **Findings:** when an automated or human review finds a defect, fix the class it belongs to, not only the case, and resolve the finding with the commit and test that fix it.

-- **`peel_expr` (`component.rs`) peels `as X` casts (and parentheses, `satisfies` and non-null assertions) before every component-detector call site, uniformly.** Real component libraries (Fluent UI, antd) commonly wrap a `forwardRef`/HOC call or a bare identifier alias in a trailing `as` cast — Fluent UI's own source notes this is required to work around the lack of distributive unions in `@types/react`. Every detector in `component.rs` that pattern-matches a `CallExpression` or bare `Identifier` init goes through this peel first, so the cast itself never has to be special-cased per detector.
+- **`peel_expr` (`component.rs`) peels `as X` casts (and parentheses, `satisfies` and non-null assertions) before every component-detector call site, uniformly.** Real component libraries (Fluent UI, antd) commonly wrap a `forwardRef`/HOC call or a bare identifier alias in a trailing `as` cast — Fluent UI's own source notes this is required to work around the lack of distributive unions in `@types/react`. Every detector in `component.rs` that pattern-matches a `CallExpression` or bare `Identifier` init goes through this peel first, so the cast itself never has to be special-cased per detector. What counts as a wrapper is one exhaustive match (`wrapper`, no wildcard arm), so a new expression kind in a later OXC release fails to compile instead of being skipped; `peel` also looks through an instantiation and returns its type arguments (OXC 0.159 keeps `(f<T>)(x)` and `extends (B<T>)` as a `TSInstantiationExpression`), and a callee, a call's type arguments and an `extends` target are read only through `callee_of`, `call_type_arguments` and `super_class`. import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

base_bin, head_bin, out_dir = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
root = os.path.expanduser("~/.cache/caliper/corpora/repos")
corpora = [
    "mantine/packages/@mantine/core/src",
    "chakra-ui/packages/react/src",
    "shadcn-ui/apps/v4",
    "ant-design/components",
    "react-spectrum/packages",
]
os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)


def strip(value):
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {k: strip(v) for k, v in value.items() if k != "stats"}
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [strip(v) for v in value]
    return value


def diagnostics(value, found):
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        if "code" in value and "severity" in value:
            found.append((str(value["code"]), str(value["severity"])))
        for v in value.values():
            diagnostics(v, found)
    elif isinstance(value, list):
        for v in value:
            diagnostics(v, found)
    return found


for corpus in corpora:
    src = os.path.join(root, corpus)
    results = {}
    for label, binary in (("base", base_bin), ("head", head_bin)):
        path = os.path.join(out_dir, corpus.replace("/", "_") + f".{label}.json")
        with open(path, "w") as out:
            run = subprocess.run([binary, "extract", "--json", "--quiet", "--no-cache", "-s", src],
                                 stdout=out, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, cwd=src)
        with open(path) as f:
            data = json.load(f)
        found = diagnostics(data, [])
        semantic = sorted({d for d in found if "SEMANTIC" in d[0].upper() and d[1].lower() != "info"})
        results[label] = (run.returncode, strip(data), found, semantic)
    (bexit, bdata, bdiag, bsem), (hexit, hdata, hdiag, hsem) = results["base"], results["head"]
    new_codes = sorted(set(hdiag) - set(bdiag))
    gone_codes = sorted(set(bdiag) - set(hdiag))
    dropped = bool(bsem or hsem)
    identical = bdata == hdata
    print(f"{corpus}: exit base {bexit} head {hexit}; identical {identical}; semantic non-info base {bsem} head {hsem}"
          f"{' (run dropped)' if dropped else ''}; new diagnostic kinds {new_codes}; gone {gone_codes}")

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

base_bin, head_bin, out_dir = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
root = os.path.expanduser("~/.cache/caliper/corpora/repos")
corpora = [
    "mantine/packages/@mantine/core/src",
    "chakra-ui/packages/react/src",
    "shadcn-ui/apps/v4",
    "ant-design/components",
    "react-spectrum/packages",
]
os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)


def strip(value):
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {k: strip(v) for k, v in value.items() if k != "stats"}
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [strip(v) for v in value]
    return value


def diagnostics(value, found):
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        if "code" in value and "severity" in value:
            found.append((str(value["code"]), str(value["severity"])))
        for v in value.values():
            diagnostics(v, found)
    elif isinstance(value, list):
        for v in value:
            diagnostics(v, found)
    return found


for corpus in corpora:
    src = os.path.join(root, corpus)
    results = {}
    for label, binary in (("base", base_bin), ("head", head_bin)):
        path = os.path.join(out_dir, corpus.replace("/", "_") + f".{label}.json")
        with open(path, "w") as out:
            run = subprocess.run([binary, "extract", "--json", "--quiet", "--no-cache", "-s", src],
                                 stdout=out, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, cwd=src)
        with open(path) as f:
            data = json.load(f)
        found = diagnostics(data, [])
        semantic = sorted({d for d in found if "SEMANTIC" in d[0].upper() and d[1].lower() != "info"})
        results[label] = (run.returncode, strip(data), found, semantic)
    (bexit, bdata, bdiag, bsem), (hexit, hdata, hdiag, hsem) = results["base"], results["head"]
    new_codes = sorted(set(hdiag) - set(bdiag))
    gone_codes = sorted(set(bdiag) - set(hdiag))
    dropped = bool(bsem or hsem)
    identical = bdata == hdata
    print(f"{corpus}: exit base {bexit} head {hexit}; identical {identical}; semantic non-info base {bsem} head {hsem}"
          f"{' (run dropped)' if dropped else ''}; new diagnostic kinds {new_codes}; gone {gone_codes}")

1	## What
2	
3	Bumps the oxc crates 0.158 -> 0.159 (dependabot) and fixes the two detection regressions the bump caused, at the class level.
4	
5	**What changed in OXC 0.159** (diff of `oxc_ast` and `oxc_parser` 0.158.0 vs 0.159.0 in the cargo registry):
6	
7	- `oxc_parser` now splits an instantiation's type arguments onto the enclosing node only when the instantiation is unparenthesized (`split_unparenthesized_instantiation`, "as in TypeScript"). 0.158 split it whatever the parentheses. Under our `preserve_parens: false` this changes four shapes:
8	  - call: `(f<T>)(x)` is now `CallExpression { callee: TSInstantiationExpression(f, T), type_arguments: None }` (was `callee: f, type_arguments: T`)
9	  - heritage: `class C extends (B<T>)` is now `heritage.expression: TSInstantiationExpression(B, T)`, `heritage.type_arguments: None`
10	  - `new (A<T>)()`: `new.callee` is a `TSInstantiationExpression`
11	  - tagged template `(f<T>)`...``: `tag` is a `TSInstantiationExpression`
12	- `oxc_ast`: the only type change is a new `label_id` field on `LabelIdentifier` (labels; not read by us).
13	- Parser behaviour with no effect on what we read: a string followed by an operator or member access is no longer a directive; `as`/`satisfies` before `**` stops the expression; numeric-separator diagnostics; lexer and checkpoint refactors. `ParseOptions`/`preserve_parens` unchanged.
14	
15	**Fix: one normalisation for every callee and `extends` read** (`crates/core/src/extractor/component.rs`):
16	
17	- `wrapper(expr)`: the one list of what a type-only wrapper is (parentheses, `satisfies`, `!` pass the type; `as`, `<T>x` replace it; `f<T>` gives type arguments). It matches `Expression` exhaustively, so the next OXC release that adds an expression kind fails to compile here instead of silently skipping it.
18	- `peel(expr) -> Peeled { expr, type_arguments, identity }`: beneath every wrapper, with the outermost instantiation's type arguments unless an `as`/`<T>x` above it replaced the type, and whether an assertion replaced the callee's type (review round 3, below).
19	- `callee_of(call)`, `call_type_arguments(call)` (the call's own, else the instantiation's), `super_class(class)` (target and type arguments through the wrappers).
20	- `peel_expr` (values) is now defined over the same list and gains `<T>x`. Since review round 5 it also reads through an instantiation (`memo(List<Row>)`, `(List<Row>)!`): the type arguments are needed only at callee and `extends` sites, which use `peel`.
21	- Every site that read `call.callee`, `call.type_arguments` or `class.heritage` for detection now goes through these: `try_forward_ref`, `try_hoc_wrapped` (memo(forwardRef)), `is_forward_ref_call`, `extract_callee_name`, `is_object_assign_call`, `is_component_wrapper_call`, `super_class_is_component_family`, `try_class_component`, visit.rs's class skip diagnostic, `react_api` (now takes the call, so no caller can pass a raw callee), wrapper.rs (`try_record_wrapper_call`, tagged factory, `call_names_props_type`, `wrapper_callee`, `try_record_factory_call`, element type argument evidence), interface.rs (Object.assign scan, `Root.Item = memo(...)`), uses.rs (`record_call`), evidence.rs (render-evidence callee names, hook calls, PascalCase calls). `try_fc_annotation` and `try_class_expression_wrapped` now peel their initializer too.
22	- Not changed, and why: `body_facts::through_wrappers` already climbs through `TSInstantiationExpression`; `new` callees and tagged-template tags are not read for detection.
23

## What

Bumps the oxc crates 0.158 -> 0.159 (dependabot) and fixes the two detection regressions the bump caused, at the class level.

**What changed in OXC 0.159** (diff of `oxc_ast` and `oxc_parser` 0.158.0 vs 0.159.0 in the cargo registry):

- `oxc_parser` now splits an instantiation's type arguments onto the enclosing node only when the instantiation is unparenthesized (`split_unparenthesized_instantiation`, "as in TypeScript"). 0.158 split it whatever the parentheses. Under our `preserve_parens: false` this changes four shapes:
  - call: `(f<T>)(x)` is now `CallExpression { callee: TSInstantiationExpression(f, T), type_arguments: None }` (was `callee: f, type_arguments: T`)
  - heritage: `class C extends (B<T>)` is now `heritage.expression: TSInstantiationExpression(B, T)`, `heritage.type_arguments: None`
  - `new (A<T>)()`: `new.callee` is a `TSInstantiationExpression`
  - tagged template `(f<T>)`...``: `tag` is a `TSInstantiationExpression`
- `oxc_ast`: the only type change is a new `label_id` field on `LabelIdentifier` (labels; not read by us).
- Parser behaviour with no effect on what we read: a string followed by an operator or member access is no longer a directive; `as`/`satisfies` before `**` stops the expression; numeric-separator diagnostics; lexer and checkpoint refactors. `ParseOptions`/`preserve_parens` unchanged.

**Fix: one normalisation for every callee and `extends` read** (`crates/core/src/extractor/component.rs`):

- `wrapper(expr)`: the one list of what a type-only wrapper is (parentheses, `satisfies`, `!` pass the type; `as`, `<T>x` replace it; `f<T>` gives type arguments). It matches `Expression` exhaustively, so the next OXC release that adds an expression kind fails to compile here instead of silently skipping it.
- `peel(expr) -> Peeled { expr, type_arguments, identity }`: beneath every wrapper, with the outermost instantiation's type arguments unless an `as`/`<T>x` above it replaced the type, and whether an assertion replaced the callee's type (review round 3, below).
- `callee_of(call)`, `call_type_arguments(call)` (the call's own, else the instantiation's), `super_class(class)` (target and type arguments through the wrappers).
- `peel_expr` (values) is now defined over the same list and gains `<T>x`. Since review round 5 it also reads through an instantiation (`memo(List<Row>)`, `(List<Row>)!`): the type arguments are needed only at callee and `extends` sites, which use `peel`.
- Every site that read `call.callee`, `call.type_arguments` or `class.heritage` for detection now goes through these: `try_forward_ref`, `try_hoc_wrapped` (memo(forwardRef)), `is_forward_ref_call`, `extract_callee_name`, `is_object_assign_call`, `is_component_wrapper_call`, `super_class_is_component_family`, `try_class_component`, visit.rs's class skip diagnostic, `react_api` (now takes the call, so no caller can pass a raw callee), wrapper.rs (`try_record_wrapper_call`, tagged factory, `call_names_props_type`, `wrapper_callee`, `try_record_factory_call`, element type argument evidence), interface.rs (Object.assign scan, `Root.Item = memo(...)`), uses.rs (`record_call`), evidence.rs (render-evidence callee names, hook calls, PascalCase calls). `try_fc_annotation` and `try_class_expression_wrapped` now peel their initializer too.
- Not changed, and why: `body_facts::through_wrappers` already climbs through `TSInstantiationExpression`; `new` callees and tagged-template tags are not read for detection.

Invariants: a wrapper is recognised by an exhaustive match (allow-list, no wildcard); type arguments are taken from an instantiation only through type-preserving wrappers; a value-position instantiation is read as its base (review round 5; round 1 kept it unread), and since round 6 its type arguments bind the component's type parameters where they can, with a `GENERIC_ARGUMENT_MISMATCH` warning where they cannot.

`extract` output is identical to oxc 0.158 on all five corpora (below). The new reads only add forms that were never detected before (a cast or `!` on a callee or `extends` target, a wrapped class expression, `<T>x` in `.ts`); `.changeset/wrapped-component-forms.md` says so (lead's round, below).

## Evidence

- Wrapper matrix test `extractor::wrapper_matrix_tests` (new): 16 detection forms (React.forwardRef, forwardRef, forwardRef with a typed render function, React.memo, memo, memo(forwardRef) with inner and outer callee wrapped, class extends React.Component / PureComponent, class expression, arrow, function expression, React.FC annotation, export default forwardRef / memo / class) x 9 callee/heritage wrappers (none, parenthesised, `(f<T>)`, `((f<T>))`, `as`, `satisfies`, `!`, `(f<T>)!`, `<T>x`) and 6 value wrappers (none, parens, `as`, `satisfies`, `!`, `<T>x`), each in `.tsx` and `.ts` (type assertions `.ts` only). Each row asserts the full serialized `ComponentMapping` (name, props type, type args, param defaults, rule, wrapper callee; spans dropped) equals the unwrapped form's, the baseline is `Button`/`Props`, and no parse error.
  - On the dependabot head (df33c646): 112 rows fail, including both reported forms (`React.forwardRef [InstantiationInParens]`, `class extends React.Component [InstantiationInParens]`) in `.tsx` and `.ts`.
  - With the fix: passes.
- Mutation proof:
  - `call_type_arguments` without the instantiation fallback: 30 rows fail (forwardRef, memo, memo(forwardRef), export default forwardRef with `(f<T>)`, `((f<T>))`, `(f<T>)!`).
  - `super_class` without the instantiation's type arguments: 24 rows fail (all class forms with those wrappers).

## Review round 3 (Entire reviewer on 5cc72430; fixed in d03206f6, changeset in 30126f66)

**Root cause.** All three findings come from one assumption: that peeling an assertion (`as`, `<T>x`) off a callee is harmless. It is not. An assertion replaces the callee's type, so the callee's name and its declared signature stop describing the call. `satisfies`, `!` and parentheses keep the type. The matrix only tried `as typeof f`, which keeps the type, so it never met an assertion that changes what the call means.

**Design** (`component.rs`):
- `Peeled` now carries `identity: Identity::{Kept, Replaced(&TSType)}`. `Kept` means no assertion was crossed, or every one is `typeof` the same expression (identifier or static-member chain, itself unwrapped), `any` or `unknown`. Any other assertion gives `Replaced` with the outermost such type. This is an allow-list.
- `Peeled::keeps_identity()` means the callee's declaration describes the call. It is required for every declaration read.
- `Peeled::named()` means the callee's name still describes the call. It holds when the identity is kept, or when the replacing type leaves the result named but unresolved: a type reference (React Aria's `(forwardRef as forwardRefType)`, 97 sites in react-spectrum, read the same way on main), or a function type returning a type reference, alone or with `null`/`undefined`. Every other type (keyword, literal, object, function returning one) states a non-named result, so the call is declined. This is also an allow-list. A member also needs its namespace to hold: `(React as object).memo` is not React's `memo`.
- `named(expr)` and `callee_of(call) -> Option<&Expression>` are the only ways to read a name through wrappers.

**Root cause.** Round 2 read every assertion as transparent (over-accepting). Round 3 swung the other way: an allow-list (`keeps_identity`, `names_its_result`) declined every assertion it did not recognise, so forms that origin/main (oxc 0.158) detected were dropped with no Diagnostic. That is a recall regression, and it breaks our own rule, "unknown unless proven": an assertion may decline a candidate only on affirmative evidence that the call is no component, never because the extractor cannot read the asserted type. Finding 4 is a separate defect in the same code: `peel` re-peeled the rest of the chain for each assertion, so its cost grew exponentially with the chain length.

**Design** (`extractor/component.rs`):
- `Peeled { expr, type_arguments, evidence }`. One linear pass (`layers`) over the wrappers finds the value, the outermost instantiation's type arguments (unless an assertion sits above them) and the **outermost** assertion. Only the outermost assertion decides, because `(e as A) as B` has type `B`.
- `Evidence` has four values and one exhaustive match over `TSType` (`asserted`). No match in the new code has a wildcard arm:
  - `Identity`: no assertion, or the outermost one is `typeof` the same expression (identifier or static-member chain), `any` or `unknown`.
  - `Reference(&TSTypeReference)`: a type reference. It counts as the identity when the file declares `type F = typeof <the callee>` at module level (`typeof_aliases`, a pre-pass; a name declared twice and a generic alias are excluded). Otherwise it is `Unknown`.
  - `NotRenderable`: every call signature of the asserted type (a function type, or the call signatures of a type literal) declares a result no component or element has: a primitive or `object` keyword, `void`, `never`, a literal, a template literal, a type predicate, an object type with no call or construct signature, an array of those or of `unknown`/`any`, or a union of those with `null`/`undefined`.

- Namespace assertions: with no assertion on the callee itself, `(React as T).forwardRef` takes the type `T` declares for the member. A property's type is read like a callee assertion, and methods by their results. If `T` is `any`, `unknown` or `typeof React`, the member keeps its own type. A member that `T` does not declare is `Unknown`. This works at any depth of the member chain.
- Rules:

## Review round 7 (four findings on 33b492b9; one class fix in d25f263c) **Root cause.** This is the third round in which a form origin/main (oxc 0.158) detected is dropped. Rounds 4 to 6 classified an asserted call result with an open-ended, syntax-shaped `Returns` (`Node`/`Neither`/`Empty`/`Maybe`): "every non-callable object literal", "an array of `any`/`unknown`", "a string" were each read as hard evidence against a call. Each type shape the classifier did not anticipate (`any[]`, an element-shaped object literal) became a verdict against a real component. Finding B is the same class on the declaration side: an unavailable callee signature (absence) dropped a candidate whose props the call names. **The rule (the only way to produce `NotRenderable`).** `component::never_renders(ty)` is a closed list: the result types TypeScript cannot assign to `ReactNode | ComponentType | ReactElement` under any instantiation, read from the asserted type's own syntax with nothing resolved: - `object`, `symbol`, `void`, read through parentheses. - A callee type yields `NotRenderable` only when it is a function type, a type literal's call signatures, or a namespace member's method/property/getter declarations, and every signature's written result is on the list (`combine`: one that is not, or one with no result, makes the callee `Unknown`). - Everything else is `Unknown`: `bigint` (a member of `ReactNode` since @types/react 18.3; checked in the installed 19.3.0), `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `null`, `undefined`, literals, template literals, type predicates, `any`, `unknown`, `never`, arrays and tuples (`any[]`, `unknown[]`), object literals with or without call signatures, function and constructor types, unions and intersections (not read member by member), references, `typeof`, imports, indexed access, conditional, mapped, `infer`, `this`, type operators, `intrinsic`, JSDoc types. - `never_renders` is one exhaustive match over `TSType` with no wildcard arm, each arm group commented with why. `the_closed_list_is_one_match_without_a_catch_all_arm` reads the function's source and fails on an arm that is not a `TSType::` variant, or on a list other than three entries. - Consequences: `Returns`, `Evidence::NoComponent`, `Peeled::renderable` and `rendered_callee` are deleted; `Peeled::named()` is the one accessor (declines only on `NotRenderable`). A string or number result no longer declines `memo`/`forwardRef`/a HOC/an element factory: a string is a node, so round 5 and 6's `NoComponent` rows (`function, string`, `string | null`, literal) are now kept, as origin/main kept them. `void` moves from `NoComponent` to the closed list. - Known limit: syntax cannot see a project that augments React's `DO_NOT_USE_OR_YOU_WILL_BE_FIRED_EXPERIMENTAL_REACT_NODES` with `object`, `symbol` or `void`. **B: a wrapper whose callee is withheld keeps the candidate.** `try_record_wrapper_call` records the pending wrapper with `callee: self.wrapper_callee(call)` (an `Option`) instead of returning when it is `None`; the props its type arguments name still resolve, without the original signature. Consumers of the guard (`describes_call`): `wrapper_callee` (now kept as `None`), `try_record_factory_call` (unchanged, see Not verified) and `describes_call` itself. **Findings** (each failing test run on 33b492b9's sources with this round's tests appended): - A CONFIRMED, fixed. `a_map_asserted_to_return_any_array_still_renders_its_callback`: `(rows as { map(render: (row: string) => React.ReactNode): any[] }).map(row => {row})` gives `["List"]` (and for `unknown[]`); `object` gives `[]`. On 33b492b9: `left: []`, `right: ["List"]`. - B CONFIRMED, fixed. `an_asserted_wrapper_keeps_the_props_its_type_arguments_name`: `(ui as { withContext

(View: React.ComponentType

): React.FC

import json
import subprocess
import sys

project = "/tmp/claude-501/oxc7/fproj"
bins = {"base": sys.argv[1], "head": sys.argv[2]}
index = dict(line.split("\t", 1) for line in open(project + "/index.tsv").read().splitlines())


def run(binary):
    out = subprocess.run([binary, "extract", "--json", "--quiet", "--no-cache", "-s", "src"], cwd=project,
                         capture_output=True, text=True)
    data = json.loads(out.stdout)
    found = {}
    components = data["components"]
    items = components.items() if isinstance(components, dict) else enumerate(components)
    for key, component in items:
        text = json.dumps(component)
        row = next((r for r in index if f"/{r}.tsx" in text), None)
        name = component.get("displayName") or component.get("name") or key
        props = component.get("props")
        prop_names = sorted(props.keys()) if isinstance(props, dict) else props
        found.setdefault(row, []).append(f"{name}{prop_names}")
    diags = [d for d in json.dumps(data).split('"code"')[1:]]
    return found, data


results = {label: run(binary) for label, binary in bins.items()}
shapes = {}
for row, case in sorted(index.items(), key=lambda kv: int(kv[0].split("_")[1])):
    base = results["base"][0].get(row, ["-"])
    head = results["head"][0].get(row, ["-"])
    print(f"{case}\tbase {base}\thead {head}")

json.dump(results["base"][1], open("/tmp/claude-501/oxc7/fbase.json", "w"))

---
cargo/caliper-docgen: patch
npm/caliper-docgen: patch
---

**A component is found when its `forwardRef`, `memo` or base class is wrapped in parentheses, a cast or type arguments.** `export const Button = (React.forwardRef<HTMLButtonElement, Props>)((props, ref) => …)` and `class Button extends (React.Component<Props>) {}` list their props, where they were skipped.

- Why it matters: libraries write these forms to satisfy their own typing, and a skipped component shows no Controls.
- Covered: parentheses, `as`, `satisfies`, `!` and type arguments, around the callee or the base class, in `.ts` and `.tsx`.
- Also covered: a generic component given type arguments where it is wrapped or aliased, such as `memo(List<Row>)`, `Object.assign(List<Row>, { Item })` or `const RowList = List<Row>`, with or without a cast or `!` around it.
  - The type arguments are applied: `memo(List<Row>)` lists `ListProps<Row>`.
  - Limit: where they cannot be applied (an imported component, a type parameter used inside the props type such as `GridProps<T[]>`, a cast beneath the type arguments), the props keep the type parameters and a `GENERIC_ARGUMENT_MISMATCH` warning names the component.
- Nothing to adopt: output for components that were already found is unchanged.
- Limit: a cast drops a component only when it says the call returns `object`, `symbol` or `void`, which React cannot render and no component is: `(memo as (c: unknown) => object)(…)` is not listed. Every other cast is read as the plain call, including one whose result is a string, a number, `any[]`, an object type such as `{ type: string; props: {}; key: string | null }`, a union or a type reference.
- Limit: only a cast to the callee's own type (`typeof` the callee, a `type Factory = typeof createButton` alias, `any` or `unknown`) keeps the callee's declaration. A generic wrapper cast to another signature gets the props of its render function, or the props its type arguments name (`(ui as SomeType).withContext<PublicProps>(Base)` lists `PublicProps`), not the extra props its own declaration adds. A factory cast that way (`(createButton as SomeFactory)()`) is not listed.
  - An alias counts only when the file declares its name once at the top level as a type: a factory cast to an alias that is also imported or merged with an interface is not listed. The same name declared again inside a namespace, function or class, or as a type parameter, hides the alias only for a cast inside that scope.

## Review round 8 (the factory rows round 7 left declined) **Classification** (data: `/tmp/claude-501/oxc7/factory-probe.txt`, from `/tmp/claude-501/oxc7/fprobe.py`: release builds of origin/main f4a88f93 and this head, `extract --json --quiet --no-cache --load-dependencies` on a scratch project with React's types): - **The 90 differential rows lose nothing in output.** The differential's factory (`function createButton(): React.FC`) is never published by origin/main, even unasserted, because a non-generic function with a declared result records no function result. Origin/main and this head both publish no component for all 110 factory rows. The 90 rows differ only in the extractor's mappings (`Button:createButton` on main, none here). - **The real regression is a rendering factory**, `function createButton() { return (props: Props) =>
; }`. Origin/main lists `Button` with `label` through every assertion. This head drops it for 11 shapes: `as F`, `as typeof other`, `as object`, and calls asserted to return `React.FC`, `React.ComponentType`, `React.FC | null`, a callable literal returning `React.FC`, `string`, `React.ReactNode`, `unknown` and `object`. Only `=> object` is a correct decline (closed list). Main's `label` is right at runtime, since the value is `createButton`'s component. - A generic factory asserted to another signature (`(createButton as F)()` for `function createButton(): React.FC`) is not listed by origin/main either, so it is no regression. **What this round changes** (`extractor/wrapper.rs`, `try_record_factory_call`): the drop is no longer silent. When an assertion replaces a factory callee's type and the evidence is not `NotRenderable`, the binding's one `SKIPPED_CANDIDATE` says why: "'Button' is built by a call to 'createButton' through a type assertion that replaces its type, so the declaration that would give its props is not read and it is not listed". It replaces the generic "matched no known component pattern" message, so there is still one skip per candidate. A result on the closed list (`=> object`, `=> void`) keeps the generic skip. The plain and `typeof`-kept calls are listed with no skip. **Why not the real answer here:** the resolver needs both the original callee (is the value a component?) and the asserted result (where its props come from), and `ComponentMapping` carries one callee. The fix needs `ComponentMapping.asserted_result: Option`. `ComponentMapping` is part of the cached `SourceData` (`cache/golden.rs`), so it is a cache format bump. It goes in its own PR after #523 merges: read the asserted signature's result (`React.FC

`, `ComponentType

`, a type reference) for props the way a declared result is read today; when that result names no component, list the component with the props the call site supplies and a diagnostic that the declaration was not read. **Evidence (round 8):** - `a_factory_called_through_an_assertion_says_why_it_is_not_listed`: exact `(component names, SKIPPED_CANDIDATE messages)` for the plain call and `typeof` itself (`Button`, no skip), the 10 withheld shapes (no component, the message above, once), and `=> object`/`=> void` (no component, the generic message only). `a_typeof_alias_is_shadowed_only_where_its_name_is_declared_again` now expects the specific message for its module-level redeclaration rows. - Mutation proof (`/tmp/claude-501/oxc7/mutate8.py`, 2 of 2 killed): no reason for a withheld callee fails both tests; giving the reason on the closed list too fails the new one. - Output: identical to origin/main (oxc 0.158) on all five corpora (same method and counts as round 7), no new diagnostic kind, no run dropped. - Gates by exit code: `just lint doc-check machete typos` 0; `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast` (sandbox off) 0, 1762 passed, 3 skipped, no snapshot changed; `just test-checker-lane` (sandbox off, no `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`) 0. - `.changeset/wrapped-component-forms.md`: limit added: a component built by a rendering factory called through a type assertion is reported with a `SKIPPED_CANDIDATE` diagnostic instead of props. ## Not verified - Round 8: the 11 rendering-factory shapes stay unlisted (with the diagnostic) until `ComponentMapping.asserted_result` lands in its own PR. The differential's factory form is one origin/main never publishes; the follow-up should switch it to a rendering factory so the table bounds real output.
